b: I introspect a lot, probably more than is useful some days. One thing I keep coming back to is how many of the "fix this about yourself" notes introverts get are the same trait, just seen on a bad day.
Taking a while to answer in a meeting reads as unprepared. On a good day it's the person who actually thought before talking.
Skipping the big group thing reads as antisocial. On a good day it's the same person who keeps two or three friendships going for years.
Going quiet after a long day reads as moody. On a good day it's someone who knows when they're done and leaves before they get short with people.

In personality research introversion is a spot on a scale, not a defect, and where you sit on it says nothing about whether you're good with people. So the useful question is probably not how to stop being like this, but where the trait tips over. Taking time to answer is fine until you stop answering at all. Small groups are fine until you haven't seen anyone in a month.
Which of yours gets read as a flaw but works in your favour when the day goes right?
